dossier.public_summary: The dip changes dramatically between visits, odd and even events have very different depths, and only a few deep events drive the signal - all typical of an eclipsing binary or blended false positive, not a steady planet transit on this star.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits have strongly different depths (6.6 sigma) pointing to an eclipsing binary at twice the reported period, not a planet.
reasons.value: diff_sigma 6.596, depth_odd_ppm 86.04 vs depth_even_ppm 299.5, depth_difference 0.7128 depth_difference_ppm 213.5 depth_ratio 3.5

reasons.why: Depth is not constant; SPOC 2-min p_constant 6.742047269639952e-16 and QLP sector depths vary far beyond errors, inconsistent with a stable planetary transit.
Signal is driven by a few very deep events; the majority of shallow/nondetections and one -455 ppm outlier are incompatible with a planet.
reasons.value: share_of_top_3 0.913, p_consistent 3.7671478211602886e-67, chi2 374.575686897399 dof 20, 968 ppm at epoch -56 sigma 12.1

reasons.why: Duration is long for the star size and density match is poor with grazing geometry; supports a stellar-eclipse interpretation.
